interpretation: The native land shader uses baked per-vertex E/k COLOR. Sector-local first-liquid-material selection, byte packing and original interpolation are preserved by reading retained original sector arrays, not approximating with terrain_cells or current water depth.

A lazy contact-only RGBA8 atlas keeps 33x33 vertices per sector, including duplicate edges. Existing cover geometry/RID remains unchanged. These two maps have no differing adjacent-edge values, so they do not alone exercise a mismatched sector seam.

Candidate01 adds E/k to native vertex or enhanced fragment lighting, and the existing remaining native-point fallback. Optional local-light addition retains native absence of E/k. Candidate02 reuses the native point-contribution helper structure; both strict controlled same-input point pixels clear. This does not identify the compiler arithmetic cause.

Final ordinary shoreline comparison: 65 checks, two retained failures. Original sun/point light mismatches fall 5596/6375 to zero; enhanced sun/point fall 5698/6595 to 230/217, not full parity. All four E/k input cases clear 6899 baseline mismatches at unchanged 1e-5 threshold. Controlled nonzero-emissive helper comparisons pass at 1e-7. Light comparison remains 0.002; no tolerance relaxation.
All twelve native D, E/k and native E/k-omitted captures are byte-identical between baseline and final candidate. Baseline 65/12 and first 65/4 candidate remain retained.

Source proves this caused a 0.00005694m edge mismatch; the corrected fixture reads actual indexed vertices, with unchanged tolerances, mesh and placement. Failed edge runs remain retained.

The authored bridge witness has nonzero k but zero E and lies above the liquid plane. The scene isolates only copied-ground input texture values; it is not an underwater crossing, physical walking, native point/shadow equivalence or general quality claim.

Outside-band, upper-object, silhouette, held and restoration controls are exact.
